option_relations.rationale: Cutaneous metastatic breast carcinoma is a broader category that includes breast carcinoma cutaneous metastasis with intravascular invasion.
Carcinoma erysipeloides is a clinical presentation of cutaneous metastasis from breast carcinoma, which can include intravascular invasion.

Telangiectatic metastatic breast carcinoma (TMBC) directly describes the clinical and histopathological findings of breast carcinoma cutaneous metastasis with intravascular invasion, as telangiectasia is a key feature and intravascular invasion is implied by the telangiectatic appearance.

Carcinoma en cuirasse is a sclerodermiform variant of breast carcinoma metastasis, which presents with induration and hardening of the skin, not primarily telangiectasia and intravascular invasion as described in the vignette and leaf.
